title: Tech Note: Creating Mashups in the 4D Ajax Framework Client
author: Jason T. Slack, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note walks through building a Web 2.0-style 'mashup' — embedding a Google Maps view triggered from address data — inside the 4D Ajax Framework Client using a Developer Defined Window (DDW) that opens external HTML/URL content and a small 4D method that constructs a Google Maps URL from record fields. It captures a snapshot of 2007-era rich-internet-application thinking built on 4D's now-discontinued Web 2.0 Pack/4DAF product and the classic Google Maps URL API, both of which have been superseded by 4D's built-in Web Server, modern JS frameworks, and current mapping APIs/embed methods; the specific DAX_Dev_DDW_GetAttributes commands and 4DAF Portal/Settings UI no longer exist in current 4D. The general mashup concept (combining external web content/APIs with local data) remains a standard web development pattern today, just implemented very differently.
related_updates: The 4D Ajax Framework (4DAF) and 4D Web 2.0 Pack subscription products, including Developer Defined Windows, have been discontinued and removed from current 4D releases
Modern 4D web/mobile projects would integrate mapping APIs (e.g. Google Maps JavaScript API) directly via the built-in Web Server, REST/ORDA data access, or a custom web component rather than a DDW
